rule: Sea-ice locking, Marson et al. (2024), JGR Oceans 129, e2023JC020697, https://doi.org/10.1029/2023JC020697

parameters.note: paper defaults, not tuned on this data

run_order: v1-v4 and the first sensitivity grid: scored 2026-11-24, first run

v5, v6 and the force-balance grid: added the same day after reading the paper's PDF. P_s in the paper is |F_c+F_p+F_r+F_a+F_o|/W (its Eq. 3); v3/v4 used the Eq. 2 drag form from a mis-transcribed brief. No parameter was changed. v1-v4 are checked unchanged on every run.
differences_from_paper: berg dynamics are WDE17 (closed form), not NEMO-ICB
daily sea-ice fields (day 0 of each CMEMS cycle), not model time steps
ramp denominator is (v_s - v_t); the printed Eq. 5 has (v_t - v_s)
v3/v4: P_s is the Eq. 2 drag form, not the paper's P_s
v5/v6: P_s is the paper's Eq. 3 on WDE17's forces (Coriolis, pressure gradient, water drag), for a berg held at the ice velocity, with an assumed 250 m berg thickness
an unlocked berg feels no sea-ice drag (WDE17 has no such term)
caveats: USNIC positions are accurate to only a few km
weekly fixes: no track between them, no beacons
keel draught and berg thickness are assumed, USNIC publishes neither

sea_ice.source: CMEMS GLO12 day 0 of each archived cycle (data/cmems_forecast_archive)

v1_wde17.description: WDE17 on CMEMS analysis surface currents, zero wind

v2_grounding.description: v1 + grounding (assumed keel 208 m on IBCSO)

v3_sil.description: v1 + sea-ice locking with the drag-form P_s (not the paper's; in effect locking on concentration alone)

v5_sil_force_balance.description: v1 + sea-ice locking with the paper's P_s (force to hold the berg at the ice velocity)

sensitivity.note: v3 re-run on a grid; shown as sensitivity only. The headline is the paper-default run. No parameter was chosen from this.

sensitivity_force_balance.note: v5 re-run on the same grid; sensitivity only.
